sections.title: An introduction to eigenvalues and eigenvectors
Diagonalization, similarity, and powers of a matrix
Markov chains and Google's PageRank algorithm

variables.meaning: a square n × n matrix whose eigenvectors and eigenvalues are sought, such as [1 2; 2 1]; the matrix of the rental-car system x_{k+1} = Ax_k
an eigenvector of A, a nonzero vector with Av = λv for some scalar λ, so that v and Av lie on the same line
a second eigenvector of A = [7 6; 6 −2], w = [−1, 2], with Aw = −5w
the eigenvalue associated to an eigenvector v, the scalar λ with Av = λv; the scalar of a multiple λv of a vector
the eigenvalue associated to the eigenvector v₁
the eigenvalue associated to the eigenvector v₂
the first of two eigenvectors v₁, v₂ of a 2 × 2 matrix A, which form a basis of ℝ²; [1, 1] for A = [1 2; 2 1], [3, 1] for the rental-car matrix
the second of two eigenvectors v₁, v₂ of a 2 × 2 matrix A; [−1, 1] for both A = [1 2; 2 1] and the rental-car matrix
a vector written as a linear combination of eigenvectors, x = v₁ − 2v₂, so that Ax = 3v₁ + 2v₂ is found by scaling each term
the state vector of a discrete dynamical system at time k; the vector x_k = [P_k, Q_k] of the number of cars at the two locations at the end of day k, carried to the next day by x_{k+1} = Ax_k
the initial state of a discrete dynamical system; the vector x₀ = [1000, 0] of cars on Monday morning, written as the linear combination 250v₁ − 250v₂ of eigenvectors
the weights c₁, c₂ of a linear combination c₁v₁ + c₂v₂ of eigenvectors, which A multiplies by the eigenvalues
the diagonal matrix [3 0; 0 −1], which stretches vectors horizontally by a factor of 3 and flips them vertically; the matrix A is equivalent to it when viewed in a basis of eigenvectors
the kth power of the matrix A, which carries the initial state x₀ of a discrete dynamical system to the state after k steps; Aᵏv = λᵏv for an eigenvector v
the number of days elapsed, the index of the state vector x_k and the exponent of (0.2)ᵏ
the number of rows and of columns of a square matrix, the measure of its size in counting the effort of row reduction
the first of the two locations, P and Q, of the car rental company
the second of the two locations, P and Q, of the car rental company
the number of cars at location P at the end of day k, the first component of x_k
the number of cars at location Q at the end of day k, the second component of x_k
a square n × n matrix whose eigenvalues are the roots of its characteristic polynomial det(A − λI) and whose eigenvectors are the null space of A − λI
an eigenvector of A, a nonzero solution of the homogeneous equation (A − λI)v = 0
an eigenvalue of A, a solution of the characteristic equation det(A − λI) = 0; the variable of the characteristic polynomial
the eigenvalues λ₁, λ₂, …, λₙ of an n × n matrix, the n roots of its characteristic polynomial, some possibly complex and some repeated; λ_j is the jth of them, with multiplicity m_j
the eigenspace of A associated to the eigenvalue λ, the subspace Nul(A − λI) formed by the eigenvectors associated to λ
the identity matrix, whose product with any vector x is Ix = x
the determinant of the matrix A − λI, which is zero exactly when λ is an eigenvalue; as a function of λ, the characteristic polynomial
the null space of a matrix; Nul(A − λI) is the eigenspace E_λ
the dimension of an eigenspace E_λ, at least 1 and at most the multiplicity of λ
the rank of a matrix A, the number of pivot positions in A; dim Nul(A) = n − rank(A)
the multiplicity of an eigenvalue λ, the number of times λ − λ′ appears as a factor of the characteristic polynomial; 1 ≤ dim E_λ ≤ m
the multiplicities m₁, m₂, …, m_p of the eigenvalues λ₁, λ₂, …, λ_p in the characteristic equation (λ₁ − λ)^{m₁}(λ₂ − λ)^{m₂}…(λ_p − λ)^{m_p} = 0
the number of distinct eigenvalues λ₁, λ₂, …, λ_p of a matrix
the number of rows and of columns of a square matrix, which is the degree of its characteristic polynomial and the number of its eigenvalues counted with multiplicity
the imaginary unit, i² = −1, in the complex eigenvalues λ = i and λ = −i of the 90° rotation
a basis of ℝⁿ consisting of eigenvectors of A, such as 𝓑 = {[1, 2], [2, 3]} for A = [−4 4; −12 10]
the vector multiplied by the matrix A, whose components are the weights of the linear combination Ax of the columns of A; a nonzero solution of the homogeneous equation Ax = 0
a basis vector v_j chosen for each eigenspace E_{λ_j}; together, when the eigenvalues are real and distinct, a basis of ℝⁿ
a square n × n matrix diagonalized as A = PDP⁻¹ when it has a basis of eigenvectors, or similar to a rotation and scaling C when it has a complex eigenvalue
the invertible matrix P = [v₁ v₂ … vₙ] whose columns are a basis of eigenvectors of A, so that AP = PD and A = PDP⁻¹; expressed in the basis defined by its columns, A has the same effect as D
the inverse of the matrix P of eigenvectors, the last factor of A = PDP⁻¹
the diagonal matrix whose diagonal entries are the eigenvalues λ₁, λ₂, …, λₙ of A, with A = PDP⁻¹; its powers Dᵏ are found by raising the diagonal entries
the kth power of the diagonal matrix D, whose diagonal entries are λ₁ᵏ, λ₂ᵏ, …, λₙᵏ, so that Aᵏ = PDᵏP⁻¹
the kth power of the matrix A, which carries the initial state x₀ to the state after k steps; Aᵏ = PDᵏP⁻¹ when A = PDP⁻¹
the inverse of the square matrix A; A⁻¹ = PD⁻¹P⁻¹ when A = PDP⁻¹ is invertible
an eigenvalue of A; a complex eigenvalue λ = a + bi of a 2 × 2 matrix
the first eigenvalue of A, the first diagonal entry of D and the eigenvalue of the first column of P; the complex eigenvalue 1 + i chosen to form C
the second eigenvalue of A, the second diagonal entry of D; the conjugate eigenvalue 1 − i
the eigenvalues λ₁, λ₂, …, λₙ of A, the diagonal entries of D
the first vector of a basis of eigenvectors of A, the first column of P, with eigenvalue λ₁
the second vector of a basis of eigenvectors of A, the second column of P, with eigenvalue λ₂
the eigenvectors v₁, v₂, …, vₙ that form a basis of ℝⁿ, the columns of P
the state vector of the rental-car system at the end of day k, x_k = Aᵏx₀
the initial state [1000, 0] of the rental-car system
a matrix to which A is similar, A = PBP⁻¹ for an invertible matrix P
the matrix C = [a −b; b a] to which a 2 × 2 matrix with the complex eigenvalue a + bi is similar; it rotates vectors by θ and scales them by r
the matrix C′ = [1 1; −1 1] formed from the other complex eigenvalue λ₂ = 1 − i, which rotates vectors by −45° and scales them by √2
the matrix P′ = [1 −1; 2 −1] with A = P′C′P′⁻¹
the real part of the complex eigenvalue λ = a + bi, the upper left entry of C; a = r cos θ
the imaginary part of the complex eigenvalue λ = a + bi; b = r sin θ
the imaginary unit, i² = −1, in the complex eigenvalue λ = a + bi
the distance from the origin to the point (a, b), r = √(a² + b²), the factor by which C scales vectors
the angle formed by the point (a, b) with the positive horizontal axis, through which C rotates vectors
the exponent of a power Aᵏ or Dᵏ, the number of steps of a dynamical system
the number of rows and of columns of a square matrix, the number of eigenvectors in a basis of ℝⁿ
the matrix of a discrete dynamical system x_{k+1} = Ax_k, whose eigenvalues and eigenvectors determine the long-term behavior of the trajectories; A = PDP⁻¹ or A = PEP⁻¹
the state vector of a discrete dynamical system at time k, such as the populations x_k = [R_k, S_k] of two species in year k, with x_{k+1} = Ax_k and x_k = Aᵏx₀
the initial state vector, such as the initial populations x₀ = [2, 3], written as a linear combination of the eigenvectors of A
a state vector, written in the coordinates {x}_𝓑 of the basis of eigenvectors so that {Ax}_𝓑 = D{x}_𝓑
the coordinates of a state vector x_k in the basis 𝓑 of eigenvectors, {x_k}_𝓑 = [1.3ᵏ·2, 0.5ᵏ·1], scaled at each step by the eigenvalues
the basis 𝓑 of ℝ² or ℝ³ formed by the eigenvectors of A, whose coordinate system turns the system into the diagonal one
the matrix P = [v₁ v₂] whose columns are the eigenvectors of A, with A = PDP⁻¹ or A = PEP⁻¹; Activity 4.4.3's P = [1 −1; 1 1]
the inverse of P, which converts standard coordinates into the coordinates of the basis of eigenvectors
the diagonal matrix of eigenvalues, D = [1.3 0; 0 0.5], whose phase portrait is drawn in the eigenvector coordinates
the simpler matrix with A = PEP⁻¹, diagonal when the eigenvalues are real and a rotation and scaling [a −b; b a] when they are complex, whose phase portrait is drawn on the left
the eigenspace E_{λ₁} of the eigenvalue of largest absolute value, the line or subspace to which the trajectories of a saddle converge; E_1.3 for the two species, E_1.1 for the 3 × 3 systems
an eigenvalue of A, real or complex λ = a + bi, whose absolute value against 1 decides the type of the dynamical system
the first eigenvalue of A, 1.3 for the two species, whose absolute value is compared with 1 in classifying the system
the second eigenvalue of A, 0.5 for the two species
the third eigenvalue of a 3 × 3 system, 1.1, into whose eigenspace the trajectories converge
the eigenvector v₁ = [2, 1] of the two-species matrix, with eigenvalue 1.3, whose line the trajectories approach
the eigenvector v₂ = [−2, 1] of the two-species matrix, with eigenvalue 0.5
the third eigenvector of a 3 × 3 system, a basis vector of E_1.1
the eigenvectors v_j of A, which replace the standard basis vectors e_j in the phase portrait of A
the standard basis vectors e_j, the axes of the phase portrait of the diagonal matrix D
the weights of the initial vector x₀ as a linear combination c₁v₁ + c₂v₂ of eigenvectors, multiplied by λ₁ᵏ and λ₂ᵏ after k steps
the real part of a complex eigenvalue λ = a + bi; a² + b² against 1 decides between a spiral repellor, a center and a spiral attractor
the imaginary part of a complex eigenvalue λ = a + bi
the first of two interacting species, R and S, the predator in a predator–prey system
the second of two interacting species, R and S, the prey in a predator–prey system
the population of species R, in thousands, after k years, the first component of x_k
the population of species S, in thousands, after k years, the second component of x_k; the ratio R_k/S_k approaches 2
the number of juvenile female bison, less than one year old, in year k
the number of yearling bison, between one and two years old, in year k
the number of adult bison, older than two years, in year k
the number of years elapsed, the index of the state vector x_k and the exponent of λᵏ
a parameter of a dynamical system in the exercises: the second eigenvalue of D = [p 0; 0 1/2], or the rate at which species R preys on S

a stochastic matrix, a square matrix whose columns are probability vectors; the transition matrix of a Markov chain x_{k+1} = Ax_k, such as the rental-car matrix [0.8 0.4; 0.2 0.6] or the voting matrix
the stochastic matrix B = [0.4 0.3; 0.6 0.7], positive, with eigenvalues 1 and 0.1, whose Markov chains converge to q = [1/3, 2/3]
the stochastic matrix C = [0 0.5; 1 0.5], positive because C² has all positive entries
the stochastic matrix D = [0 0.5 0; 1 0.5 0; 0 0 1], not positive, with two steady-state vectors
the matrix with A = PEP⁻¹ for the voting matrix, E = [1 0 0; 0 0.4 −0.2; 0 0.2 0.4], the rotation and scaling of the complex eigenvalues beside the eigenvalue 1
the Google matrix of an Internet, the stochastic matrix with Gx = x whose entry in row i and column j is the share of page j's PageRank given to page i
the modified Google matrix G′ = αG + (1 − α)Hₙ, a positive stochastic matrix whose Markov chains converge to the PageRank vector
the n × n matrix all of whose entries are 1/n, a positive stochastic matrix describing a jump from any page to any other with equal probability
the 1 × n matrix S = [1 1 … 1] of the exercises, whose product with a vector adds its components, so that Sx = [1] for a probability vector and SA = S for a stochastic matrix
the kth term of a Markov chain, a probability vector giving the distribution of cars, voters or PageRank after k steps, with x_{k+1} = Ax_k
the initial probability vector of a Markov chain, such as x₀ = [0.4, 0.3, 0.3] for the voters or e₁ for a Markov chain of PageRank
the PageRank vector x = [x₁, x₂, …, xₙ] of an Internet, the steady-state vector of its Google matrix, Gx = x
the PageRank x_j of page j, the jth component of the PageRank vector, which measures the quality of the page
a steady-state or stationary vector of a stochastic matrix A, a probability vector with Aq = q, to which a Markov chain converges when A is positive
a basis vector of the eigenspace E₁, such as v = [1, 2, 2] for the voting matrix, whose scalar multiple with entries adding to 1 is the steady-state vector
the eigenspace of the eigenvalue λ₁ = 1 of a stochastic matrix, Nul(A − I), in which the steady-state vectors lie and into which the trajectories of a Markov chain are pulled
an eigenvalue of a stochastic matrix, with |λ| ≤ 1
the first eigenvalue of a stochastic matrix, λ₁ = 1, which every stochastic matrix has
the second eigenvalue of a stochastic matrix; a Markov chain may fail to converge when |λ₂| = 1, as for [0 1; 1 0]
the third eigenvalue of the voting matrix, 0.4 − 0.2i, the conjugate of λ₂
the eigenvalues other than λ₁ = 1 of a stochastic matrix, which satisfy |λ_j| ≤ 1, and |λ_j| < 1 when the matrix is positive
the scalar for which cv, a multiple of a basis vector of E₁, is a probability vector; c = 1/5 for v = [1, 2, 2]
the parameter mixing G and Hₙ into the modified Google matrix G′ = αG + (1 − α)Hₙ, thought to be 0.85 at Google: the probability that a user follows a link rather than jumping to a random page
the number of pages of an Internet, the size of the Google matrix and of Hₙ
the number of steps taken in a Markov chain, the index of x_k
the first of the two rental locations P and Q, or of the three political parties P, Q and R
the second of the two rental locations P and Q, or of the three political parties P, Q and R
the third of the three political parties P, Q and R
the number of cars at location P on day k; the percentage of voters voting for party P in election k
the number of cars at location Q on day k; the percentage of voters voting for party Q in election k
the percentage of voters voting for party R in election k
